title: Nathan Fielder lookalike contest crowns a deadpan winner
summary: Dozens competed in a Nathan Fielder lookalike contest in Toronto on Tuesday, taking on business pitches, a staring contest and an improvised conversation with an Elizabeth Holmes impersonator.

image.caption: Comedian and filmmaker Nathan Fielder, left, inspired a lookalike contest at Toronto’s Paradise Theatre on Tuesday, which was won by Jayden Daniels, right, who never broke character once onstage. (Chris Delmas/AFP via Getty Images, Mehrdad Nazarahari/CBC)

blocks.text: Entertainment·New
Dozens competed in a Nathan Fielder lookalike contest in Toronto on Tuesday, taking on business pitches, a staring contest and an improvised conversation with an Elizabeth Holmes impersonator.
30 contestants competed for the title at Toronto’s Paradise Theatre

Dozens of Nathan Fielder lookalikes delighted a packed audience of comedy fans at a Toronto Theatre on Tuesday night to answer a simple, if oddly specific question: Who looks most like Nathan Fielder?

Thirty contestants sporting grey wigs took part in the competition devoted to the Canadian comedian and filmmaker with the unnervingly earnest persona — known for the docu-comedies Nathan for You, The Rehearsal and the recent hit documentary You Can See Everything.
The lookalikes came dressed for the role, with some wearing headphones and button-down shirts, while others leaned into Fielder’s signature blank stare and dry delivery.

But resemblance was only part of the assignment. Over the course of the evening at the Paradise Theatre, they faced a business pitch challenge, a staring contest and a final conversation with an Elizabeth Holmes, the disgraced tech executive at the centre of You Can See Everything, impersonated by Second City alumnus Hannah Spear.

The pitch round produced schemes worthy of Nathan For You, in which Fielder plays an awkward business consultant fielding extreme, absurd marketing ideas to help real struggling businesses. One lookalike contestant named David, a drummer, proposed growing his indie band's audience on Instagram without paying for ads. He said the band had 250 followers, "and statistically 40 of those are my mom’s friends" before presenting a QR code to follow the band.
Another pitch was for a celebrity lookalike contest in which winners would pay rather than collect prize money. "This is not a prize list. This is a price list," said one contestant.

Host Andrew Phung, known for Kim’s Convenience and Run the Burbs, welcomed the crowd with a suitably grand introduction, calling Fielder "a cultural icon, a Canadian pop culture phenomenon and a graduate of one of Canada’s top business schools with very good grades" — a playful nod to the opening tagline of Nathan for You and to the fact that Fielder really did earn a business degree from the University of Victoria in 2005.
Phung and Spear judged the contest alongside Kelly White and Megan Bianco, hosts of the Nathan for Us fan podcast.
Thirty contestants and fans of awkward comedy filled the Paraside Theatre on Tuesday. (Christine Pagulayan/CBC)

The judges narrowed the group to three finalists, evaluating each contestant’s appearance, costume, physicality, business pitch and improv skills. Toronto’s Jayden Williams took the crown, after staying in character throughout the competition.
"There were some Nathan ringers out there," Daniels told CBC News. "I’m shocked and flattered that I won."
Daniels said friends had repeatedly sent him a photo of the event flyer until he finally decided to enter. He also had experience: he’d already won two Halloween contests dressed as Fielder.

When asked about staying in character throughout the competition, Daniels responded with a pause and a deflection worthy of the comedian he was impersonating: "I really, I don’t know what you’re talking about."
Daniels, centre, said he’d already won two Halloween contests dressed as Fielder. (Lucky Osunbiyi Photography)

The contest attracted both longtime fans and people who had only recently discovered the comedian. Some were hooked by Fielder’s deadpan delivery; others found his comedy compelling precisely because it feels a little unsettling.
"He scares me, and that’s why I like him," one attendee said. Fielder, the fan added, seems "like an alien on Earth that’s pretending to be human."
Another fan called him "Canadian excellence," adding that his older work had found a wider audience as his profile grew.
After the winner was crowned, the crowd settled in to watch the first episode of The Curse, Fielder’s series with Benny Safdie.

items: Loved You Can See Everything? Thank Canada
Nathan Fielder's You Can See Everything gazes into the abyss of Elizabeth Holmes

blocks.text: The contest arrived amid renewed attention around Fielder’s work, including You Can See Everything, the hit documentary co-directed with Lance Oppenheim that examines disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes. Fans at the theatre said the film had introduced them to Fielder or deepened their interest in his work.

Fielder lookalike contests have also been held in cities including New York, Los Angeles and Sydney. But for one night, Toronto’s many Nathans shared a stage, and one went home with the title, "the Nathanest Nathan," as dubbed by those on social media.
Daniels said he hoped to see more lookalike contests across more Canadian cities, including Montreal and Hamilton. "But it was nice to have one in Toronto, with one of Canada’s heroes," he said.
